name: What if the last contractor did bad work and I want to restart the whole-house renovation?

mainEntity.name: What if the last contractor did bad work and I want to restart the whole-house renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: A prior contractor’s incomplete or poorly documented work should be disclosed before new design or construction begins. Gather contracts, invoices, plans, inspection records, warranties, photographs, product information, and a timeline of known defects. The new team may need to verify concealed work rather than rely on another contractor’s representations. Elite Remodeling & Design can use the available record and site conditions to clarify the scope, but unresolved safety or quality concerns should be identified before finishes are selected.
acceptedAnswer.description: Provide every available contract, plan, invoice, inspection record, warranty, photo, and defect note before requesting a new scope. Existing work may need inspection or selective opening because documentation cannot confirm concealed quality. Separate repair, removal, and new construction costs so the plan is transparent.
